en.name: Dried tofu (pressed bean curd)
en.summary: Despite the name, 豆干 is not a dry food — it is pressed, still-moist bean curd and spoils like fresh tofu. Keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below for 5–7 days, or freeze it for 3–5 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Both figures are read across from tofu; no agency publishes one for 豆干.
en.pantry: Not a room-temperature food, whatever the name suggests. Pressed bean curd has had water squeezed out of it, but it is still a moist, low-acid, high-protein soy product, and fresh soy products are among the most perishable things in a Taiwanese market. Anything left out is in the danger zone of 4–60 °C (40–140 °F) and follows the two-hour rule, one hour if the kitchen is above 32 °C (90 °F). Buy it from a chilled counter and get it home cold.
en.fridge: 5–7 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, sealed, and go by the printed date when there is one — it should win over any general figure. This range sits between the published figure for plain tofu and the roughly one week that the Japanese tofu-products guidance gives pressed and fried bean-curd products. Marinated and braised versions — 滷豆干, 五香豆干 — go slimy on the surface first, which is the warning sign to watch for: discard at the first sour smell rather than rinsing it off and hoping.
en.freezer: 3–5 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and 豆干 freezes better than fresh tofu because it holds much less water, so there is less ice to rupture the curd. Slice or shred it before freezing, both because a frozen block is hard to cut and because thin pieces thaw evenly. Kept continuously frozen it stays safe well beyond that window; the limit is drying, freezer burn and a firmer, chewier texture on thawing.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge, or add shredded pieces straight to a hot pan or a simmering braise from frozen. Never thaw on the counter. Pieces thawed in the fridge and still at or below 4 °C (40 °F) may be refrozen with some quality loss.
spoilage: A sour or fermented smell, which is decisive — do not rinse and use it anyway.
A slimy or sticky film on the surface, especially on marinated types.
Cloudy or ropy liquid in the pack.
Any mould, or a pink or grey discolouration.
tips: Buy it chilled and keep it chilled; the name is misleading.
Go by the printed date over any general figure.
Slice or shred before freezing so it thaws evenly and cuts cleanly.
Marinated 豆干 spoils sooner than plain — the braising liquid adds sugar and moisture.

faq.q: How long does 豆干 keep?
faq.a: 5–7 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 3–5 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Go by the printed date when there is one.
No. Despite the name it is pressed, still-moist bean curd and spoils like fresh tofu. It belongs in the fridge.
Yes, 3–5 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and it freezes better than fresh tofu because it holds less water. Slice or shred it first.

zh.name: 豆干
zh.summary: 名字雖然有個「干」，豆干並不是乾貨——它是壓過水、仍然濕潤的豆製品，壞起來和嫩豆腐一樣。請放 4 °C 以下 5～7 天，或 −18 °C 冷凍 3～5 個月。這兩個數字都是比照豆腐而來；沒有機關為豆干公布期限。
zh.pantry: 不管名字怎麼寫，它都不是常溫食品。豆干只是把水壓掉了一部分，本質上仍是含水量高、低酸、高蛋白的黃豆製品，而新鮮黃豆製品是台灣市場裡最容易壞的東西之一。擺在外面的就在 4～60 °C 的危險溫度帶裡，適用兩小時原則，廚房超過 32 °C 時只有一小時。請在冷藏櫃買，並且低溫帶回家。
zh.fridge: 密封放 4 °C 以下 5～7 天；包裝上有印製日期就以日期為準，那應該勝過任何通用數字。這個區間介於公布的嫩豆腐期限，和日本豆腐製品指引給壓製與油炸豆製品的「約一週」之間。滷過、五香的那些會先從表面發黏，那就是要注意的警訊：一聞到酸味就丟掉，不要沖一沖就繼續用。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 3～5 個月；豆干比嫩豆腐耐凍，因為它含水少得多，能撐破凝乳結構的冰也少。冷凍前先切片或切絲，一來凍硬的整塊很難切，二來薄片解凍得比較均勻。只要全程沒退冰，超過這段時間仍然安全；限制它的是變乾、凍燒，以及解凍後變得更緊實、更有嚼勁的口感。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍，或把切絲的直接從冷凍下熱鍋、丟進滷鍋裡。絕對不要在檯面上解凍。在冷藏解凍、且維持在 4 °C 以下的可以再冷凍，只是品質打折。
spoilage: 聞到酸味或發酵味，這是決定性的——不要沖一沖就將就用。
表面出現黏滑的膜，滷製品尤其明顯。
包裝裡的湯汁變濁或可以牽絲。
出現任何霉，或轉成粉紅、灰色。
tips: 在冷藏櫃買、全程保持低溫；這個名字會騙人。
有印製日期就以日期為準，不要只看通用數字。
冷凍前先切片或切絲，解凍均勻也好切。
滷豆干比白豆干更快壞——滷汁帶進了糖和水分。

faq.a: 4 °C 以下冷藏 5～7 天，或 −18 °C 冷凍 3～5 個月。包裝上有日期就以日期為準。
不行。名字雖然叫「干」，它其實是壓過水、仍然濕潤的豆製品，壞起來和嫩豆腐一樣，該放冰箱。
可以，−18 °C 下 3～5 個月，而且比嫩豆腐耐凍，因為含水量低。先切片或切絲再冷凍。
